transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Afternoon, thank you for calling S-Net broadband support, you're speaking with Leah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: hi Leah, yeah it's Farzana calling. I'm ringing up to claim the one hundred pound Wi-Fi and broadband speed guarantee credit because my speeds have been dreadful for a full thirty days now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, okay Farzana, let's get your account pulled up first so we can check the speed history on your line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: sure, uh I've kept a log of every single test I ran since the eighteenth of September because your sales team promised me a guaranteed minimum of 85 megabits on Fibre 150.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we look at the test log, Farzana, please confirm your four-digit security PIN and the first line of your home address.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: yeah my security PIN is 4482, and the first line of my address is 923 Vicarage Road, Watford.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks, that's verified on the screen now, Farzana. Tell me what you've been experiencing on your Fibre 150 connection over the past month.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: well when I signed up in August, my contract clearly stated a Minimum Guaranteed Download Speed of 85 megabits per second, and if it stays below that for thirty days I get a hundred pounds credit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Uh-huh, and when did you first log the fault with us on the portal?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I logged the speed fault in the S-Net app on the eighteenth of September, thirty days ago today, because my speed tests were only getting 18 megabits per second.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, let me just make sure I've got the summary of what you're claiming here, Farzana.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So to recap, you're on our Fibre 150 tariff which carries an 85 megabit minimum download threshold, you logged a speed fault thirty days ago on the eighteenth of September, and you're calling to claim the one hundred pound Speed Guarantee bill credit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: yes that's exactly right. Thirty days have passed since I reported that I was only getting 18 megabits, and the speed hasn't improved at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, I will run the full thirty-day line sync audit and check the router telemetry myself right now, Farzana, rather than transferring you. First I need to ask a few technical questions about how you ran those tests.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: okay ask away, I've got my laptop right in front of me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Were you running those speed tests over a wireless Wi-Fi connection or with a physical Ethernet cable plugged straight into the back of the S-Net Hub?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: over Wi-Fi on my laptop, because nobody carries an Ethernet cable around the house in 2026.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And which room of the house was the laptop in when you ran the tests, and where is your main S-Net Hub router located?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: the main S-Net Hub is plugged into the master socket in the front hallway, and I work at my desk out in the back conservatory.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you have any S-Net Wi-Fi mesh discs or third-party plug-in boosters between the front hallway and the back conservatory?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: no I don't have any mesh discs or boosters. When I bought Fibre 150, I wasn't sent any discs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And last question on the setup, Farzana: did you run the tests using a browser site like Ookla on the laptop, or did you run the hub-to-exchange test inside the S-Net app?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I did both! I clicked the speed checker inside the S-Net app on my phone and I also ran Ookla on my laptop in the conservatory.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait there while I pull the thirty-day Openreach DLM sync table from the exchange database.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, the exchange sync table has loaded up on my terminal now, Farzana.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: you vanished for ages there without telling me I was going on hold, Leah, I thought the line had cut out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Openreach database takes forty seconds to query a thirty-day rolling log. Now I'm looking at the daily router sync readings from the eighteenth of September through to today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: and what does it show? Because trying to do video calls from the conservatory has been a complete nightmare all month.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at the hub-to-cabinet sync log, Farzana, your S-Net Hub in the front hallway has been syncing at between 148 and 152 megabits per second every single day for the last thirty days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: what? 148 megabits? How can the hub be syncing at 148 megabits when my laptop and phone in the conservatory are crawling along?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because sync speed is the physical fibre speed arriving at the S-Net Hub in your front hallway over the Openreach line, whereas your laptop is connecting over Wi-Fi through walls.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: wait so you're saying the S-Net app test I ran on the eighteenth of September logged the router speed, not my device speed?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me open the diagnostic ticket from the eighteenth of September and inspect the two parts of the test log—the router-to-exchange reading and the device-to-router reading.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: yes look at the device-to-router reading on that ticket, because the app itself told me my speed in the conservatory was awful!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am also going to run a live GEA line diagnostic test and check the 2.4 gigahertz and 5 gigahertz wireless channel congestion on your hub right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: okay run that test then.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm triggering the live hub telemetry poll now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, the live hub poll has finished and I have the radio channel table open here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: again, nearly a minute of dead silence! A little warning before you mute your headset would be nice.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The radio poll locks my screen while it scans your router, Farzana. Looking at your S-Net Hub 4, both the 2.4 gigahertz and 5 gigahertz bands are currently merged under a single SSID.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: yeah whatever default settings the hub came with out of the box is what it's running on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because both bands share the same wireless name, your laptop in the conservatory has dropped onto Channel 1 on the 2.4 gigahertz band where six neighbouring routers are overlapping.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: okay well how is overlapping channels with my neighbours my fault when I'm paying S-Net forty-two pounds a month for Fibre 150?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can also see the signal attenuation between the front hallway master socket and your laptop in the conservatory is sitting at -79 dBm through the internal brick wall.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't know what -79 dBm means, Leah, all I know is the download speed I've been getting for thirty days is nowhere near the 85 megabits minimum on my contract.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what download speed were you actually getting on the test?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I literally told you twice at the beginning of the call that I was getting 18 megabits per second! Were you not listening to me at all?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I was looking at the router sync column which says 149.4 megabits, Farzana, the device column is on a separate tab in the diagnostic log.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: well open the separate tab then! You'll see 18 megabits on the eighteenth of September, 17.5 megabits on the twenty-fifth, and 18 megabits again this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I see the device-to-router readings around 18 megabits on that second tab now. And I have just pushed a channel split and wireless power reset to your S-Net Hub from here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: okay well pushing a wireless reset today doesn't change the fact that thirty days have elapsed since I logged the fault on the eighteenth of September.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, Farzana, the thirty-day Speed Guarantee bill credit of one hundred pounds does not apply to your account because your line sync speed never dropped below 85 megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: excuse me? When I took out Fibre 150 online, the big banner on your website said '85 Mbps Speed Guarantee or £100 money back'! It didn't say 'only if you sit in the hallway'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Section 4.2 of the S-Net Fibre Speed Guarantee terms states that the 85 megabit minimum threshold is measured at the router WAN port over the physical fibre line to the exchange.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: how does speed at the router WAN port help me when I'm using Wi-Fi on my laptop in the conservatory and getting 18 megabits for an entire month?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because standard broadband packages do not guarantee wireless throughput through brick walls and glass conservatories without the Whole Home Wi-Fi Plus add-on.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: nobody told me I needed a Whole Home Wi-Fi Plus add-on! Your app let me log a speed guarantee fault on the eighteenth of September when it saw 18 megabits!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The app lets anyone click the log fault button, Farzana, that doesn't mean the billing system qualifies a wireless drop-off for a one hundred pound payout.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, when I clicked log fault in the S-Net app on the eighteenth of September, it literally started a thirty-day Speed Guarantee countdown clock on my phone screen!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That countdown clock in the app just tracks thirty days from when a customer opens a speed ticket so an automated line check can run at day thirty.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And at day thirty the automated check should see that my laptop in the conservatory is still getting 18 megabits instead of 85 megabits!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The automated check at day thirty only reads the Openreach WAN sync speed to the router in the hallway, which passed at 149.4 megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: if the app accepted my fault log at 18 megabits and counted down thirty days on my screen, then S-Net owes me the one hundred pound credit you advertised!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is a completely stupid argument, Farzana—the speed guarantee only covers sync speed to the router, not wireless speed to your old laptop in the conservatory!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: did you seriously just call my argument stupid?! And insult my laptop?! Who on earth do you think you're talking to, Leah?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am stating the technical fact of how broadband works, Farzana. No telecom provider in the country pays out a line speed claim because a conservatory has weak Wi-Fi signal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: you called what I said a completely stupid argument! That is outrageous customer service, and I know for a fact this call is being recorded.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look, I have already reconfigured your S-Net Hub wireless channels so the 2.4 gigahertz and 5 gigahertz bands are separated and set to Channel 36 and Channel 6.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't care what channel you set it to when you talk to paying customers like dirt! And did changing the channel magically give me 85 megabits in the conservatory?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: With a -79 dBm attenuation reading through the external house wall into the conservatory, separating the bands will stabilize the connection around 30 to 35 megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: 30 to 35 megabits is still less than half of the 85 megabits I was promised when I signed an eighteen-month contract with S-Net!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you want guaranteed wireless speeds in every room including a conservatory, you have to add Whole Home Wi-Fi Plus for seven pounds a month, which supplies up to three mesh discs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: so instead of giving me the one hundred pound credit I'm owed after thirty days of 18 megabit speeds, you're trying to charge me another seven pounds a month?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am telling you what product covers room-to-room wireless speed, Farzana. The one hundred pound Speed Guarantee claim on ticket reference SPD-90812 has been formally rejected.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: well a manager can certainly review the recording of you calling me stupid on this call! Give me the complaint reference right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have logged your dissatisfaction against ticket SPD-90812 and complaint reference CMP-331094 on your account at 923 Vicarage Road, Farzana.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: CMP-331094. I've written that down and I am going straight to the Ombudsman with my screenshots of the thirty-day app countdown.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The ticket reference SPD-90812 and complaint CMP-331094 are both recorded on your account. Is there anything else regarding your Fibre 150 line today, Farzana?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: no! I wouldn't ask you for another thing after the way you spoke to me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right then, the wireless settings on your hub are updated. Thank you for choosing S-Net, goodbye.
